# The site's own defects, and the bugs filed for them

The read of the site found what is wrong with it: broken links, pages served under an error, an address of the
site that takes no connection, slow pages, missing security headers, and more.

- `KNOWN-ISSUES.md`: each, with why it matters, the likely fix, every page that shows it, and how the suite treats
  it. Its last section is the team's own, kept by every rebuild.
- `AUDIT.html`: the same, as one page for the site's owner. `crew`, then "Open the site's audit".

## The bugs in bugs/

A defect a test of the suite's own would trip on is filed as a bug, in `bugs/open/`. While it is open, the tests it
breaks are reported as blocked by it, not failed, so a red run still says at a glance whether anything else broke.
A run that sees the defect gone says so at its end.

- A rebuild from a new read of the site that no longer finds the defect closes the bug; a line goes into
  `bugs/FIXED.md`.
- You close one by moving its file to `bugs/closed/`; its tests count again. A rebuild that still finds the defect
  files it again, so it is looked at again.
- Nothing is sent to a tracker on its own: a bug report is yours to write, from the failing test's evidence.

## Pages that are twins

`SITE-GRAPH.md` lists pairs of pages that look like one page copied. Each is tested on what it shows, so a change
made to one and not the other passes both: when one changes, look at the other.
